_meta.scope: Film-wide costume system: character x occasion x period matrix, one default costume per character, explicit costume-change points hung on story_timeline events. Covers every character in bible/characters/index.json (44 entries incl. told-only CHAR-tortoise).
_meta.schema_note: Platform convention characters[].outfits[] (read by services/runtime/core.py _costume_entries). Outfit ids use the skeleton's COS-NNN prefix, so costume sheets are named sheet_<COS-id>.png. The skeleton's flat costumes[] list is replaced by this nested form; do not add a parallel flat list (the parser would read both).

_meta.change_point_rule: Every outfit switch is listed in its character's change_points: after_event = last event in the old outfit's range; effective_from_event = first event the new outfit is on screen. All costume switches in this film happen off screen between scenes, so storyboard/shot-planning never needs a switch inside a generation group. Wet, sooty, leaf-strewn or accessory states are NOT outfit changes: they are variants listed under the outfit and their on/off events are in the character's variant_points for 07-directing/continuity-planning.
global_rules: Period lock 1862 (style CR-002): natural fabrics only (cotton, muslin, wool, silk, velvet, linen, leather, straw); hooks, buttons, laces and ties only; no zips, plastics, synthetic sheen or post-1862 cuts.

SUP-002 / CR-003: dream figures are human performers in 1862 dress; animal and card coding is carried by colour, trim, cut and small accessories (feather collar, shell-pattern cape, webbed or split mitts, card tabard). Faces always visible: no masks, animal heads, fur suits or attached ears. Ear-like hair shapes belong to appearance cards, not costume.
SUP-004 card figures: the House of Hearts pack shares one card-back design, 'crimson-and-cream lattice card-back pattern with a small heart rosette', on the back of every tabard or panel (ch008-p16).

Palette accents (style.json palette_logic.accent_rules): cornflower blue is Alice's alone; Hearts crimson belongs only to the House of Hearts household (Queen, King, Knave, gardeners, soldiers, officers, executioner, Fish-Footman, royal children, the White Rabbit's herald tabard). Visiting monarchs, courtiers of Diamonds, Lory and crabs use scarlet, brick or coral, never Hearts crimson.

CR-010 / DEF-p3-char-index-902 / SUP-014: no axe, block, sword, noose or any execution device is part of any costume, and none is named in any visual_en (negation words are also kept out of visual_en; bans live in prohibited_in_prompt).
Size changes (SUP-003) never change a costume: forced-perspective scaled sets carry the size; production builds matching duplicate costumes for any scaled double.
Weapons and hand props (pocket watch, fan, trumpet, scroll, hookah, paintbrush, slates, sack, batons, wands, teacup, pepper-box) belong to 06-art/prop and are not part of any visual_en.

outfits.label: Blue summer frock and white pinafore

White cotton pinafore over it with bib, frilled shoulder straps, back sash bow and one deep front patch pocket (comfits and thimble live there). White stockings, black flat ankle-strap shoes, bare-headed.

outfits.visual_en: an 1862 royal procession in card costume: ten elegant courtiers, ladies and gentlemen, in scarlet-and-gold court dress, crinoline gowns and tail coats, covered by flat ivory playing-card panels with bright red diamond pips and stitched all over with small red diamond-shaped paste ornaments; and ten small children in ivory card tunics and pinafores with crimson heart pips over crimson-and-white children's dress, girls in short full skirts with white pantalettes, boys in tunic suits, with many little crimson heart appliques; the backs of all panels in a crimson-and-cream lattice card-back pattern with a small heart rosette; festive and immaculate
components: courtiers: Diamonds panels Ace, Two to Ten over scarlet-and-gold court dress, red diamond paste ornaments
royal children: Hearts tunics Ace to Ten over crimson-and-white children's dress, heart appliques

outfits.visual_en: visiting 1862 playing-card monarchs in their own suit colours: the King and Queen of Clubs in black and ivory, the King and Queen of Diamonds in scarlet and gold, the King and Queen of Spades in black and slate grey, each robe cut as a stiff flat rectangular card panel bearing its suit symbol and edged with ermine, over 1862 court dress, crinoline gowns for the queens and knee breeches with tail coats for the kings, gilt openwork crowns and small coronets each with its suit symbol at the front, the backs of the robes in a crimson-and-cream lattice card-back pattern with a small heart rosette; stately and rich

outfits.materials: silk, velvet, ermine trim, gilt metal

outfits.visual_en: an old-fashioned 1862 senior household servant's livery in dark crimson and black: a long, slightly too-tight dark crimson wool coat with black facings, a black-edged red heart badge and a plain black rank bar at the breast, a black waistcoat straining over a paunch, black knee breeches, black stockings and heavy buckled black shoes, and a black cloth hood worn pushed right back off the head so it lies on his shoulders like a cowl; empty-handed; well-worn and a little shiny at the seams

black-edged heart badge and black rank bar
black cloth hood pushed back onto the shoulders
